description: Core shall encode and decode all Syncthing BEP message types from the vendored schema so a plain Syncthing peer can complete a session without a Syncpeer-specific protocol.
notes: Uses the unmodified vendored Syncthing bep.proto.

description: Core shall frame BEP messages with Syncthing's checksum-magic hello and length-prefixed envelopes and shall parse them incrementally from a byte stream.
notes: Wire-compatible framing.

description: Core shall decompress LZ4-flagged incoming BEP messages; send-side compression is not required for interoperability.
notes: Send-side compression is not implemented; peers may still send LZ4.

description: Core shall compare, merge and advance Syncthing version vectors, including concurrent detection and overflow rejection, so conflict decisions match peer expectations.
notes: Basis for conflict handling.

description: Core shall coalesce pending INDEX and INDEX_UPDATE frames by file name and keep bounded history for encrypted replicas so metadata churn cannot flood the wire.
notes: Prevents metadata churn from flooding the wire.

description: Core shall apply and acknowledge peer ClusterConfig and shall not declare a session ready before it arrives.
notes: Required before index sync.

description: Core shall apply peer INDEX and INDEX_UPDATE frames into folder state and shall bootstrap a missing empty index when a folder opens.
notes: Real Syncthing integration covered by test-local.

description: Core shall request file blocks by offset, size and hash and shall map peer response codes and timeouts to explicit transfer outcomes.
notes: Core download primitive.

description: Core shall send periodic PINGs, enforce a receive timeout and exchange CLOSE frames with a propagated reason.
Core shall enforce Syncthing's 16 MiB maximum plaintext block size on ranges it requests and plans it publishes.
notes: Guards malformed peers.

description: Core shall open a peer session by combining discovery, candidate racing, transport connect and the BEP handshake into one explicit session handle.
notes: Main entry for all apps.

description: Core shall depend only on an injectable host adapter for TLS, QUIC, relay, hashing, randomness, discovery and logging so the same client runs in CLI, desktop and Android shells.
notes: Keeps core framework-free.

description: Core shall derive device IDs from certificate DER and shall reject a peer whose certificate does not match the expected device ID.
notes: Syncthing-compatible identity.

description: Core shall emit structured diagnostics events for handshake, discovery, index, transfer and closure decisions through the host log hook.
notes: Console and native error logs retain stable events and commands but omit arbitrary messages; copied diagnostics redact peer and filesystem metadata.

description: Core shall retry safe operations after a transport closure and shall raise an explicit ambiguous-publication outcome instead of replaying an upload or deletion whose outcome is unknown.
notes: Protects against silent duplicate publication.

description: Core shall validate shared-folder uniqueness and encryption mode and shall advertise folder and device configuration with index ID, max sequence and password token.
Core shall periodically scan local replicas, receive remote indexes, request missing blocks and republish changed indexes for subscribed folders.
notes: Shared by CLI, desktop and Android.

description: Core shall serve blocks for content it has published and shall answer invalid or missing requests with the matching BEP error code.
notes: Peers can pull published content.

description: Core shall publish and consume receive-encrypted indexes without holding the folder key, validating the ciphertext replica identity and password token.
notes: Untrusted relay nodes need no folder key.

description: Core shall run all connection transitions through one explicit state machine (idle, connecting, connected, waiting, reconnecting, suspended, stopping, error) with capped randomized backoff.
notes: One state machine for all shells.

description: Core shall probe for a better connection path and shall swap sessions only after the replacement is ready, closing the old path afterwards.
Core shall suspend or resume a session based on online state, foreground state and active transfers.
notes: Android battery/network policy builds on this.

description: The session store shall expose observable session state and shall reject stale updates through request and epoch guards.
Core shall model directory browsing as explicit idle, loading, ready, stale, locked and error transitions with reload semantics.
Core shall resolve folder passwords by source device and folder ID and shall produce an explicit device-scoped password map for each connection.
notes: Behavior is exercised indirectly by credential and connection tests.

description: The app shall persist named saved devices with introducer and auto-connect metadata and shall connect to a saved device with one action.
notes: Stored per profile with secure credential rules.

description: Core shall resolve peer addresses through a Syncthing global discovery server and shall parse tcp, quic and relay candidates.
notes: Official Syncthing server or a pinned custom server.

description: Core shall consume Syncthing LAN discovery announcements and expose anonymous and device-tagged candidates; on Android the app shall hold the multicast lock while discovery is active.
notes: Android holds a multicast lock while active.

description: Core shall rank candidates with Syncthing's preference order and shall skip failing candidates through growing cooldown windows.
notes: Matches Syncthing ordering expectations.

description: Core shall support automatic, global, LAN and direct discovery plus manual candidates, racing direct candidates and delaying relay fallback.
Core shall connect through the standard Syncthing relay pool when direct paths fail or relay-only mode is configured.
notes: Fallback through the standard pool is e2e-tested.

description: Core shall connect directly over TLS with Syncthing-compatible certificates, ALPN bep/1.0 and peer certificate verification.
notes: Interoperates with real Syncthing.

description: Core shall connect over QUIC with ALPN negotiation and peer certificate extraction where the host provides node:quic.
notes: Optional Node/desktop transport.

description: Core shall accept incoming peer sessions only for approved device IDs and shall advertise the shared folders to the peer.
notes: Unknown devices are never auto-accepted.

description: Core shall serialize socket writes and shall close the socket on write failure or abort.
Core shall reuse only hash-verified cached or partial ranges and shall request only missing blocks so interrupted downloads resume without corrupting content.
notes: Includes cross-process partial recovery and encrypted ranges. A complete replacement block never authenticates a damaged prior journal chunk.

description: Core shall persist completed download ranges across retries and shall reject a download whose remote metadata changed.
Core shall download blocks with bounded concurrency, ordered writes and per-block hash verification and shall account reused, resumed and network bytes.
notes: Progress feeds the UI and notifications.

description: Core shall publish file changes with a BEP FileInfo containing chunk hashes, sequence and an advanced version vector and shall optionally await peer confirmation.
notes: Uploads buffer the whole file in memory.

description: Core shall publish a deletion tombstone with the correct encrypted name when applicable and shall optionally await the peer index confirmation.
Core shall retry transport-failing block requests and shall fall back across temporary and block-metadata modes and smaller chunked pulls for older peers.
notes: Works around older peers.

description: Core shall plan, authenticate and decrypt encrypted ranges and shall re-encrypt blocks and tokens on upload to real Syncthing encrypted folders.
notes: Verified against real Syncthing receive-encrypted data.

description: The Node download sink shall stage bytes in a temporary file, atomically replace on commit and resume verified partials across processes.
notes: Used by CLI and desktop.

description: Core shall wrap any download sink with sequential hashing and shall expose a verified digest at commit.
The app shall reduce transfer events into single or combined progress notifications with completion and cancel behavior.
The app shall cancel one transfer or all active transfers through the UI and the Android notification.
notes: Android notification cancel is device e2e tested.

description: The Android app shall run transfers under a dataSync foreground service or an Android 14 user-initiated job.
notes: Device/emulator e2e.

description: Core shall keep a large transfer active while folder metadata churns concurrently.
notes: Requires the LAN fixture.

description: Core shall publish file content through a bounded streaming path instead of buffering the whole file, including avoiding whole-file reads through the WebView bridge.
verification: streams a favorite larger than the retired service buffer cap; two Syncpeer peers exchange plaintext/encrypted blocks (streamed upload); folder CLI publication against managed Syncthing
notes: publishFileFromSource re-reads a random-access source per served block; the retired 32 MiB service buffer cap is gone.

description: The Android service shall bound favorite transfer memory, shall fail closed on oversized uploads and shall preserve the local edit in that case.
notes: Downloads stream into the document store; uploads remain capped at 32 MiB in the service isolate.

description: The Android app shall prove cached-range reuse on a device against a real peer before block reuse is claimed for Android.
notes: Desktop reuse is verified end to end; the Android provider E2E was not run.

description: The document replica shall store document bytes, logical names and private records encrypted with the folder key behind the shared replica contract.
The keyless ciphertext replica shall keep immutable generations and a journaled ciphertext index that can be received and forwarded while the folder is locked.
notes: Storage format 2 replaces the raw folder identity and password token with a domain-separated commitment; format 1 is atomically migrated under the replica lock.

description: The replica index shall hash local entries into block plans and per-device version vectors and shall retain tombstones.
The replica merge shall apply remote updates causally and shall write a Syncthing-style conflict copy when both sides changed concurrently.
notes: Converges when peers reverse edits.

description: The replica controller shall drain admitted work before pausing, resuming or closing and shall expose its state.
Core shall persist folder registrations, open their replicas and attach or detach download ownership without deleting local data on detach.
The Node folder storage shall use atomic replacement, refuse symlink parents and serialize writers through a root lock while remaining a plaintext Syncthing-compatible folder.
Core shall store replica, vault and private records in per-root WAL SQLite databases with quick_check, backups and a root identity guard.
Core shall import legacy JSON replica, baseline and pause state into SQLite and shall retire the originals only after verification; corrupt history shall never become an empty database.
notes: Corrupt legacy history is never converted to empty state.

description: Core shall talk to native byte storage through a validated command protocol and shall pack private record prefixes into native encrypted metadata.
notes: Shared by Android and desktop hosts.

description: The document filesystem shall be the single owner for vault access, folders, documents, handles, versions, create, rename, remove and sync baselines.
notes: Backs Android DocumentsProvider and desktop cache.

description: Document drafts shall persist a ciphertext base plus atomic 128 KiB changed chunks so acknowledged edits survive process death and recover as conflicts when needed.
notes: Acknowledged edits survive process death.

description: The document owner shall encrypt temporary edit blocks with an ephemeral key and shall reclaim only its own abandoned scratch.
The document owner shall persist encrypted per-source directory snapshots and cache access times within bounded caps.
Core shall enforce a bounded cache quota and shall evict by least-recent use while never evicting favorites or locally changed files.
Core shall migrate legacy plaintext cache into encrypted documents and back, verifying content before deleting originals in either direction.
The document owner shall list and restore archived versions through encrypted metadata and shall archive the current bytes as a new version on restore.
Core shall edit an existing or new replica file through scratch storage with expected-version commit and abort.
Core shall replace complete metadata snapshot loads with paged queries and shall keep blocking SQLite work off the event loop.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt; needs realistic large-catalog benchmarks.

description: A browser storage adapter shall preserve the same core storage contract if browser persistence is added.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt; no browser persistence today.

description: The root lock shall remain a coordination mechanism, not a security boundary; a hostile local process replacing directory ancestors is out of scope.
notes: Documented limitation; a crashed lock needs manual verification.

description: A synchronized folder shall keep .stfolder as its only deliberate plaintext compatibility marker.
Archived document versions shall be folder-key encrypted and shall reveal only version timing and count.
Node shall use node:sqlite, desktop and mobile shall use bundled rusqlite, Android shall call the same Rust owner over JNI, and browser persistence shall stay deferred.
All platforms shall share one metadata schema keyed by namespace and ID and shall treat stored values as opaque.
Snapshots shall be written transactionally and unchanged rows shall keep their revisions.
Storage adapters shall expose consistent SQLite snapshot backups as primitives rather than as a user-facing backup UI.
notes: Not a user-facing backup UI; backup files contain private metadata.

description: A metadata restore shall require stopped owners and matching file contents and shall never copy a database without its WAL.
notes: Restoring metadata alone does not undo document changes; never copy the database without its WAL.

description: Storage shall detect a replaced root across restarts and shall distinguish a missing database from first initialization with a sentinel.
SQLite shall run in WAL mode with FULL synchronous durability so process death rolls back partial changes.
The system shall not run old binaries or concurrent writable frontends against migrated storage.
notes: Different state roots do not share the operation lock.

description: Core shall reconcile local scans, remote listings and a durable baseline into upload, download, delete and conflict actions.
notes: Shared by CLI, desktop and tests.

description: Core shall support disabled, trash, simple and staggered version retention with age and spacing pruning across storage frontends.
Delete-everywhere shall archive local content before removal and shall propagate the deletion to the peer according to policy.
Unsubscribe shall be local-only: it shall mark the folder unsubscribed, archive and remove local contents and reset the baseline without deleting remote data.
notes: Local-only, unlike delete-everywhere.

description: The system shall define safe stale-lock recovery after an ungraceful stop and shall never treat a locked or replaced root as an empty folder.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt; a crashed lock currently needs manual verification.

description: Core shall classify paths as favorite, remote-only or ignored from exclusions and ignore patterns and shall collect qualifying descendants of favorite folders.

The Android service shall own favorite selection, transfer scheduling, durable baselines and retry state and shall reconcile selected files after connect, after document release, after favorite changes and on a bounded interval, including edits made through Android's document provider.
notes: Durable encrypted state and retry backoff.

description: Favorite sync shall propagate a deletion only while the other side matches the verified baseline, shall publish a local rename as new-path plus old-path tombstone, and shall record a conflict and preserve both copies whenever either side changed concurrently; remote renames are observed as a peer deletion of the old path.
notes: Remote renames still appear as a delete of the old path.

description: The service shall persist per-favorite phase, message, attempts and backoff encrypted so interrupted work resumes after service termination.
notes: Interrupted downloads resume from encrypted drafts.

description: The Android service shall synchronize favorite directories: it shall select remote favorite descendants plus locally cached favorites, download only selected non-ignored content, publish offline edits, and preserve local-only files.
notes: Directory rename copies descendants and tombstones old paths; unselected remote content is never downloaded.

description: Removing a favorite shall be a distinct operation from deleting a remote file or discarding a local edited copy; remote deletion happens only through the verified-baseline delete path.
notes: Excluded paths are neither downloaded nor reported; unstarring never deletes remote or local data.

description: The app shall show per-favorite phase, message and retry backoff, and shall offer retry plus keep-local or keep-remote conflict resolution that the service executes on its next pass.
notes: Resolution intent is persisted encrypted and consumed only after the operation succeeds.

description: The Android app shall explicitly register or import an existing encrypted Syncthing folder with folder-password recovery and clear peer and folder identity approval.
notes: Registration keeps the root browsable without a full download and requires explicit peer and folder approval. The API 29 clean-install emulator run passed encrypted native register/reopen/replica lifecycle on 2026-09-19; physical Android folder-password recovery remains.

description: The service shall persist encrypted directory snapshots for every visited favorite directory so a browsed favorite has an offline listing after the vault is unlocked.
notes: A never-browsed directory still has no listing; the app reports that limit plainly.

description: Mixed Syncthing and Syncpeer tests shall cover initial transfer, edits in both directions, reconnect, conflict, deletion, wrong password, tampered or truncated data and large bounded reads.
notes: Syncpeer peers cover transfer, edits in both directions, reconnect, conflict, deletion, pause/resume and identity rejection; encrypted filesystem tests cover truncation and corruption. Android plus Syncthing device runs remain.

description: The release path shall be proven on physical phones across supported Android versions for fresh install, upgrade from 0.5, offline picker access, another app's edit, background transfer, force-stop and relaunch, reboot and storage recovery, including startup-timeout and repeated-failure checks; emulator reboot is not a power-loss test.
notes: The clean-install API 29 and API 36 base emulator gate passed on 2026-09-19. On 2026-09-20 the API 29 real-Syncthing harness passed separate-editor two-way CRUD and two emulator-SIGKILL/cold-restart scenarios through the service runtime. Physical fresh-install, upgrade, true power-loss and signed-release acceptance still block release.

description: The desktop app shall wire the durable folder registry into its UI for choosing, validating, sharing and subscribing folders.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt.

description: A Linux FUSE mount shall expose the encrypted namespace as a filesystem with readiness, busy-unmount and logout behavior.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt; needs node/native lock reconciliation.

description: Windows and macOS support shall not be claimed until native SQLite, locks, markers, backups, recovery and secret protection are validated there.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt.

description: The service shall download a newly selected favorite promptly once the vault is unlocked and the session is connected, subject to transfer policy.
notes: The service triggers on favorite edits and document release; transfer policy still applies.

description: The service shall resume interrupted favorite work after Activity or process recreation, network loss and reboot using durable state and encrypted drafts.
notes: Download drafts resume byte ranges; uploads restart as a whole.

description: Registering or connecting to a folder shall not download its entire contents; its root shall stay browsable without a subscription.
notes: Roots are remembered on connect; bytes arrive only for selected favorites.

description: The 0.6 gate shall pass the five-step physical-phone scenario: create or recover a personal space and remember unlock, register a peer's encrypted folder without a full download, favorite one file and one directory, use and open the selected content offline after Activity and process restart, edit offline and exchange edits and deletions in both directions without data loss, reboot to verify remembered unlock and queued-transfer recovery, explicitly lock to require the master password, and repeat the failure cases with wrong folder passwords, corrupt metadata or blocks, interrupted large transfers and repeated service startup failure.
notes: Automated clean-install API 29/API 36 coverage passed on 2026-09-19; API 29 real-peer CRUD, interrupted replica transfer and durable offline edit across emulator SIGKILL passed on 2026-09-20. Do not tag 0.6 until the complete scenario passes on signed physical-phone builds, including upgrade, explicit-lock, corrupt-data and true power-loss cases; record devices and Android versions in release notes.

description: Upstream Syncthing fixtures shall cover wrong passwords, tampered metadata or blocks, truncation, missing data and large bounded reads.
Mixed peers shall pass directory-conflict and deletion stress tests plus physical crash and reopen checks.
Standalone folder-sync publication shall use a bounded or streaming path instead of whole-file buffering.
Core shall read and write Syncthing receive-encrypted files including filename, metadata and block encryption, verified against real Syncthing in both directions.
notes: Verified against real Syncthing in both directions.

description: Core shall implement Syncthing's untrusted folder crypto, including scrypt key derivation, AES-SIV tokens and padded XChaCha payloads, so encrypted folders interoperate.
notes: Syncthing receive-encrypted format. Block-token AES-SIV authenticates the offset plus Syncthing's trailing empty associated-data component; request validation decrypts and compares the plaintext block hash.

description: Core shall wrap BEP FileInfo in Syncthing's encrypted metadata format for wire publication and disk trailers without leaking original counters.
notes: Does not leak original counters.

description: Core shall store vault, settings, baseline and favorite state as authenticated encrypted records.
Core shall reconstruct encrypted directory structure from metadata without reading contents or retaining per-file keys.
Core shall parse encrypted trailers and journal generations so a keyless relay can forward ciphertext.
The vault shall wrap one stable random key with a master password and shall support create, unlock, lock and password change atomically; wrong passwords and corruption shall fail closed.
notes: Wrong passwords and corruption fail closed.

description: The app shall offer an explicit OS-protected remembered unlock, shall propagate remember and forget state and shall revoke access on lock.
The Android app shall protect the remembered unlock secret with biometric or device-credential authentication without exposing the secret.
A device-protected vault shall use a generated device secret instead of a user password.
The app shall produce an offline recovery backup using a distinct recovery password and shall restore the vault from it.
notes: The Folder settings page exposes export and import; device-local roots and documents are excluded from the backup.

description: Native metadata shall be stored in a SQLCipher database keyed with sqlite3_key and an HMAC key check.
notes: The native cache index and resumable-transfer metadata use a separately keyed SQLCipher store. openssl-src is locked to the latest compatible 300.5.5+3.5.5 release because OpenSSL 3.6 x86 crypto assembly is incompatible with the pinned Android NDK 26 assembler; the x86_64 Android build and emulator filesystem gate passed on 2026-09-19. Physical-device verification remains.

description: The encryption boundary shall cover legacy cache and partial-transfer metadata, UI and WebView state, the folder registry and the keyless ciphertext-history index; it shall preserve the index's required locked operation, shall document unavoidable structural leakage and shall remove old plaintext copies only after a verified migration.
notes: UI state, folder registrations, legacy credentials and native cache metadata migrate only after encrypted read-back. The keyless index stores an identity commitment; its unavoidable structural leakage is record size, generation count, opaque descriptors and names, ciphertext sizes and block layout, flags, version summaries, generation IDs/revisions and pending-state presence.

description: SAF output shall be a deliberate plaintext export, clearly identified before data is written, and shall never be presented as part of the encrypted replica.
notes: The PIM export UI identifies the selected directory as plaintext before writing; physical-device verification remains.

description: The app shall recover or explicitly re-approve the password for an existing encrypted folder.
notes: Import re-approves peer and folder identity; recovery restores scoped credentials from the personal-space backup. Physical Android verification remains.

description: The memory-hard bootstrap KDF shall run off the UI thread so creation and unlock do not freeze the interface.
verification: an injected KDF port is awaited so the caller keeps running; an injected password KDF port serves vault creation and unlock
notes: Desktop WebView derives in a short-lived worker; the Android document runtime already runs in a background isolate and keeps the in-process default.

description: The CLI device-private identity key shall be protected by the platform credential store or an encrypted identity container.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt.

description: Fresh installs shall use encrypted document storage, SQLCipher metadata and protected native identity, and legacy plaintext identity files shall fail safely.
notes: A fresh-profile test scans every native root for plaintext names and content; plaintext legacy identity files fail closed until local reset.

description: Backups, temporary files and diagnostics shall be audited against the same encryption policy as the main database.
notes: SQLCipher database, WAL and backups are ciphertext; JSON and CLI resume replacements use exclusive mode-0600 temporary files with cleanup; diagnostic consoles, native forwarding and copied logs omit arbitrary private messages and redact structured identifiers.

description: Unlock tests shall cover wrong password, missing Keystore material, process death, reboot, reset and recovery, and shall require the master password on first unlock and after explicit lock while using Keystore only when remembering was enabled.
notes: Core covers wrong password, missing remembered secret, locked device, failed rotation and occupied-profile recovery; physical-device reboot and reset runs remain in the release acceptance scenario.

description: CLI metadata shall be encrypted with a managed key.
Remaining plaintext WebView and legacy secret fallbacks shall be removed after reset is validated.
Core shall clear decrypted keys and temporary buffers when an owner locks or closes.

A personal space shall derive its bootstrap key from the master password with scrypt and wrap a random space ID, settings-folder ID and root key, supporting recovery without revealing either identifier.
notes: Hides identifiers and supports recovery.

description: The personal space shall derive the personal vault key and shared settings-folder password from the stable root key with HKDF, and changing the master password shall only rewrap that key.
notes: Changing the master password only rewraps the stable root key.

description: Owned devices shall pair with ECDH P-256, HKDF and AES-GCM, shall require matching 6-digit confirmation codes and shall expire unused invites.
notes: Transport, persistence and UI wiring remain planned.

description: The owned-device roster shall be signed and hash-chained with genesis pinning, revocation, replacement and a recovery key path.
notes: Recovery key can replace all lost devices.

description: Personal-space shares shall expand to active owned devices only and shall exclude revoked or retired identities.
Personal-space settings shall propagate as an authenticated change DAG with parent and cycle checks, tombstones and explicit conflicts.
notes: Not yet connected to BEP or the UI.

description: Pairing shall run over LAN or relay transport with persistence, stable device slots, user confirmation, revocation and BEP membership propagation.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt; primitives exist.

description: Versioned folder-share targets and device-scoped favorites shall persist in the encrypted settings folder and shall apply across owned devices.
notes: From remaining_issues.txt.

description: A usable export and import workflow shall exist for the offline personal-space backup, and it shall state that the backup contains neither downloaded documents nor device identity keys.
notes: The UI states the backup contains neither downloaded documents nor device identity keys; recovery starts with remembering disabled. Physical-device verification remains.

description: If a future release is advertised as a shared personal space, cross-device settings, pairing, revocation and favorite propagation shall become release blockers with their own recovery and compromise tests.
notes: Explicitly excluded from the Android 0.6 release promise; retain as a future release gate.

description: Personal-space recovery and compromise rekey shall be proven end to end, including mixed Syncthing interoperability and device reboot.

A future release shall provide a stable HTTPS URL that runs Syncpeer without native installation and opens an existing personal space only with the master password plus a separate space locator, recovery credential or approved-device invitation; the browser shall establish authenticated end-to-end encrypted connectivity over WebRTC data channels when available and a secure WebSocket tunnel or relay fallback otherwise, without giving the hosting or relay service plaintext access.
notes: Outside 0.6; depends on browser storage and transport adapters plus pairing and recovery wiring. Reusable secrets shall never appear in URLs, and persistence on a browser device shall require explicit opt-in. The WSS fallback may follow the same architectural pattern as Taskyon's tunnel.

description: Core shall parse, split and serialize vCard 3.0 contacts with names, phones and emails.
Core shall parse, split and serialize iCalendar VEVENT entries with UTC conversion.
PIM records shall use canonical per-record paths plus manifest, operation and tombstone sidecars with sanitized segments.
Core shall bootstrap PIM folders with contacts and calendar manifests and seed records.
PIM merge shall resolve contacts and events by timestamp, device and version lineage with tombstones and a silent-merge manifest.
The Android app shall list, create, update and delete contacts and calendar events through system providers and shall exchange them as vCard and iCalendar files in the synced folder.
notes: File-based PIM sync exists; provider import/export wiring is experimental.

description: PIM synchronization shall stay disabled until explicitly enabled.
notes: Default off.

description: The app shall let a user pick a PIM folder, initialize the layout, sync on demand and import provider .vcf and .ics files.
notes: Experimental.

description: The CLI shall list remote folders and browse their directory trees.
The CLI shall download and upload individual files with progress and transport reporting.
The CLI shall advertise, serve and synchronize selected local folders in both directions, including continuous mode.
notes: Includes continuous two-way sync.

description: The CLI shall list and restore archived versions, unsubscribe a local folder and publish explicit file deletions.
The CLI shall expose build info, local identity, local file listing and discovery probes for scripts and diagnostics.
The CLI shall accept host, port, certificate, key, remote ID, discovery mode and server, relay-only, QUIC-only, device name, folder password and timeout options.
notes: Covered indirectly by integration scripts, no dedicated flag test.

description: The desktop shell shall expose TLS, QUIC and relay sockets to the core session.
The desktop shell shall expose LAN discovery and global discovery fetch to core.
The desktop shell shall expose cache sinks with resume, range digest and copy, listing, removal and open actions.
The desktop shell shall route document operations to the packaged core document runtime.
The app shall export and restore a device identity recovery secret.
notes: App UI exists; no automated test found.

description: The desktop and Android shells shall store the remembered unlock secret and metadata key in OS-protected secret storage.
notes: Android replica storage now loads its metadata key through the platform vault; the API 29 Keystore secret survived emulator reboot and the encrypted filesystem reopened on 2026-09-19. Physical reboot and power-loss acceptance remain.

description: The app shall wipe app-owned data and protected credentials after typed confirmation without touching external folders or peers.
notes: Android clears app data; external folders and peers are never wiped.

description: The project shall build AppImage, deb and Flatpak bundles with consistent version metadata.
notes: CI publishes on version tags; no packaging test.

description: The desktop app shall show folder status, progress, pause and resume, reconnect and actionable errors.
The desktop app shall expose unsubscribe, delete-everywhere, archive and versioning and cache removal as separate controls.
The desktop app shall complete onboarding and logout and login cleanup by draining work, closing handles, unmounting and discarding keys.
The real desktop Secret Service remembered-secret lifecycle shall be validated beyond the isolated keyring fixture.

Node and native root-lock protocols shall be reconciled, or concurrent writable access prohibited, and host FUSE contract tests shall cover rename, truncate, random writes, concurrent handles, crash recovery and reopen.
iOS support shall not be claimed before app-private paths are validated on iOS.
The fresh-start reset shall be device-tested on Android process-clear and desktop cleanup.
notes: Never wipes external selected folders or remote peers.

description: The desktop app shall subscribe selected content in the foreground so the download cache stays current.
Releases shall be prepared from a clean tree with a version bump, a staged release commit, an annotated tag and metadata checks.
The headless umbrella shall run core, protocol, Syncthing integration, CLI, PIM, approval, discovery and native checks with explicit skips.
notes: Report written to .tmp/syncpeer-test-reports/headless-report.json.

description: The E2E umbrella shall run local and remote Tauri workflows including the in-app diagnostics catalog.
notes: Remote workflows need a configured dev server.

description: Every supported suite shall run a sensitive-identifier scan that fails on credentials, tokens, private keys and non-fixture identifiers.
notes: Runs before every supported suite.

description: One command shall build the Android APK and separate synthetic editor APK and run the modern service smoke plus the legacy compatibility and real-peer capability gates.
notes: The editor is a standalone no-launcher Gradle project whose generated output is ignored. The runner removes only Syncpeer's app, instrumentation package and editor before clean phases, and CDP automation selects the Activity WebView rather than the hidden runtime page. The complete API 36 smoke plus API 29 instrumentation/reboot/provider/real-peer/editor/SIGKILL command passed on 2026-09-20.

description: Build configuration checks shall assert that application and Tauri builds compile core first and that Android workflows use standard runners.
Generated diagnostics shall redact peer identifiers and filesystem metadata.
The Android app shall expose encrypted documents to the system Files app with list, stat, create, rename, delete, read and write operations without requiring an Activity.
notes: The separate no-launcher APK uses only persisted SAF access. On 2026-09-20 it created/read/modified/renamed/deleted real peer files and independently hashed a recovered 4 MiB provider document on API 29.

description: The Android app shall persist SAF directory grants and shall mirror cached files through SAF reads, writes, ranges and guarded replacement.
notes: Guarded replacement restores the previous document on failure.

description: The Android service shall own a sticky foreground sync session with restart recovery and notification status.
notes: The service resolves peer-scoped saved passwords before advertising attached encrypted replicas. API 29 real-peer ownership handoff and cold restart passed on 2026-09-20.

description: Background sync shall pause on metered networks or power-save mode unless explicitly allowed and shall resume when the constraint clears, without promising continuous background execution.

The Android app shall prefer JavaScriptSandbox when all required features exist and otherwise run the same packaged document core in a hidden service-owned WebView with private storage/network/timer ports; either host shall recover a terminated runtime.
notes: The fallback is headless and remains in the service process; it does not add UI or a second logic implementation. The API 29 real-peer gate passed on 2026-09-20.

description: Vault, remembered secret, background request and document runtime shall survive service or process restart.
notes: On 2026-09-20 the remembered encrypted-folder session resumed after emulator SIGKILL/cold restart; a measured in-progress 4 MiB replica transfer recovered without a corrupt commit and a durable offline provider edit converged after a second SIGKILL. This is emulator evidence rather than true power loss.

feature: Combined offline picker and peer workflow
description: The DocumentsProvider plus real-peer workflow shall be proven after Activity and process recreation.
notes: Passed on the API 29 emulator on 2026-09-20 against real Syncthing: separate-SAF-app two-way CRUD; a 4 MiB/32-block transfer killed after Syncthing reported 512 KiB sent, cold-restarted and verified by full provider SHA-256; and an offline provider edit killed again then converged. The normal transfer suite separately covers 128 MiB. Physical-device and true power-loss acceptance remain.

description: A self-contained validation harness shall run API 29 and API 36 Android emulators concurrently through a synthetic host peer with separate approved listeners backed by one encrypted replica, then prove file, edit and deletion convergence in both directions plus offline picker access and recovery after Activity recreation, process restart, background handoff, force-stop and network interruption.
notes: The runner must scope every ADB and WebView CDP operation to one emulator. Android is currently an outbound-only peer, so the host fixture mediates the simulated network; direct app-to-app networking would require a separate production inbound TLS/BEP listener and security design. Emulator evidence does not replace physical-phone, power-loss or upgrade acceptance. Explicitly deferred from 0.6.

description: The Android app shall open a document with the system chooser granting read and write permission.
The Android app shall hold a Wi-Fi multicast lock while LAN discovery is active.
notes: Android side is covered indirectly by the device e2e; host-side discovery has its own tests.

description: The DocumentsProvider shall remain usable after Activity and process recreation even with no network.
notes: The API 29 clean-install emulator gate passed DocumentsProvider discovery and encrypted filesystem reopen with the network workflow disabled on 2026-09-19; physical Files-app recreation acceptance remains.

description: Upgrading an installed 0.5 app shall be validated on physical phones.
The Android app shall offer an explicitly selected two-way folder mode with its own transfer policy while connecting never downloads a full registered folder.
Runtime recovery shall have startup-timeout and repeated-failure regression coverage plus retry and backoff that fails closed.
notes: Timeout and recovery failures retry after deterministic 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 second delays, then fail closed until service recreation. Successful recovery resets the budget; unsupported preferred-runtime capability selects the WebView host instead of counting the scenario as passed or failed. JVM tests and all 10 API 29 instrumentation tests passed on 2026-09-20; physical acceptance remains.

description: Replica roots shall live under noBackupFilesDir so Android automatic backup excludes them.
notes: Exclusion from backup does not itself encrypt contents.

description: The app shall configure discovery mode, host and port, remote ID, TLS identity, timeout and relay fallback.
The app header shall show connection phase, transport, target, attempt, next retry and path upgrade and shall reveal details on demand.
The app shall list connected, saved, advertised and LAN-candidate peers with add, connect and approval status actions.
The app shall offer explicit auto-accept for advertised devices and for folders introduced by introducers.
The app shall show folder statistics and directory entries with sorting, filtering and pagination.
The app shall navigate folder paths with breadcrumbs, chronological Back history and shareable deep links.
The app shall toggle directory display between list and grid layouts.
notes: UI-only feature.

description: The app shall show file-type icons and cached image thumbnails.
notes: UI-only feature.

description: The app shall upload multiple files into the current folder with progress, rate, ETA and cancel.
The app shall download or open a file with inline progress and cancel.
The app shall star and unstar files and folders and shall manage them from a favorites view.
notes: Background sync state from the service is not surfaced yet.

description: The app shall list downloaded files with size and cache time and shall open the file or its directory.
The app shall list archived versions and restore a selected version.
notes: Backend is tracked by test-document-filesystem.ts; page has no UI test.

description: The app shall keep browsed folders and peer metadata visible while disconnected with a last-seen label and an explicit clear action.
The app shall show active transfers with progress and shall cancel individual or all transfers.
The app shall support automatic, light and dark modes plus custom brand colors and an expert view.
The app shall show a first-run experimental warning once and keep it dismissed.
The app shall run one, one category or all diagnostics with expected-device-ID checks and copyable sanitized results.
The app shall show build and coarse runtime metadata, including OS version, and copy a sanitized support summary.
notes: OS metadata excludes hostname device model serial number accounts and other unique identifiers. The Android E2E APK containing the OS plugin built and passed the API 36 modern service smoke on 2026-09-21; clipboard export remains covered at the shared formatter boundary rather than by that smoke.

description: The app shall show timestamped session logs with details and shall prepend sanitized build and runtime metadata, including OS version, when copying them.
notes: Android reports its release version; the Node CLI also includes the kernel release. Native OS metadata excludes hostname device model serial number accounts and other unique identifiers.

description: The app shall edit versioning, preserve-local-changes, metered allowance, cache override, favorites and exclusions.

A fresh install whose document vault is uninitialized shall hydrate with default profile settings and no favorites without reporting an error while an existing locked vault shall keep encrypted settings inaccessible.
notes: Defaults are ephemeral until the user creates a vault; locked encrypted settings never fall back to defaults.

description: The app shall create the vault with a master password, offer optional remembering and support manual lock and unlock.
The app shall expose the experimental PIM toggles for contacts, calendar, folder mode and silent auto-merge.
The app shall persist non-private UI state while excluding remote entries, private keys and folder passwords from browser storage.
Onboarding shall set and explain the remembered-unlock choice.
notes: Creation explains the remembered-unlock choice and its restart/reboot behavior; explicit lock always requires the master password.

description: The app shall provide a graphical Trash and Versions surface for archived content.
This table shall keep the local storage and encryption summary current as remaining plaintext state is migrated.
notes: Vault state, folder registrations, credentials and native cache metadata are encrypted; the keyless ciphertext index stores only an identity commitment plus required opaque synchronization structure. User-selected cache/export payloads and CLI resume metadata remain plaintext by design/current backlog; CLI metadata encryption stays tracked separately.

description: Every Syncpeer feature shall remain Syncthing-compatible; Syncpeer extensions shall layer on Syncthing folders and BEP rather than replacing them.
notes: Review each new feature against this rule and record its compat value in this column.

description: Taskyon spaces shall use Syncpeer folder storage as their backend so a space remains Syncthing-compatible at the folder layer.
notes: Taskyon spaces are layered on Syncthing-compatible Syncpeer storage.

description: The system shall never silently replace an unverified local edit: without a verified baseline, or when both copies changed, it shall record a conflict and preserve both copies.
A normal Syncthing-compatible folder on disk shall remain plaintext by design and shall be documented as outside the Android encrypted-replica promise.
notes: Intentional plaintext for Syncthing compatibility; outside the encrypted-replica promise.

description: Two Syncpeer peers shall exchange ciphertext and normal folder updates over TLS through the same BEP path as Syncthing without a Syncpeer-only protocol.
notes: Ciphertext-only sharing is proven without folder keys.

description: Renaming a favorite directory shall copy every selected descendant to the new local prefix, publish each file under the new peer name, tombstone the old peer names and rewrite the favorite and cached paths without losing local edits.
notes: Non-empty directory rename is performed as copy-then-tombstone with partial-copy cleanup.

description: A conflicted favorite shall offer keep-local and keep-remote resolutions; the app shall persist the choice encrypted and the service shall execute it and consume the resolution only after success.
notes: Both directions re-verify hashes before replacing anything.

description: The service shall persist an encrypted directory snapshot for each visited favorite directory so browsed favorites keep an offline listing.
notes: Snapshots are bounded per folder and source by the existing catalog limits.
